steps.title: Feedback is a resonant path around the saturator
steps.body: A little adds body and a ring; a lot is a howl. It is internally limited, so it cannot run away no matter how you set it — this is safe to explore.

steps.title: Freq is where it rings
steps.body: Between 20 Hz and 2 kHz. On a snare band, tuning this near the drum's own pitch turns the effect into sustain rather than noise.

steps.title: One knob, two behaviours
steps.body: Right of centre compresses, with a program-dependent attack and release. Left of centre expands and gates. Dead centre is a true bypass, not a null setting.

steps.title: Why per-band dynamics
steps.body: Compressing before saturation evens out what the saturator sees, so the distortion stays constant as the source moves. Expanding after it does the opposite — the effect only appears on the loud parts.
